correctness.rationale: The exact first-placement partition into n disjoint windows proves the finite-n recursive identity. Endpoint and interior beta-integral asymptotics are positive and exhaustive. The cost of a one-child vertex is q, of a two-child vertex 1, with number of children s+2b=n-1; optimizing b proves the exponent for every n. The coefficient recurrence follows by dominated convergence. Independent checker replay verifies recurrences, n=2,3 constants, and direct n=3 quadratures, without purporting to prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: Perfect packing of an interval only epsilon longer than its geometric minimum is a natural rare jamming event. The theorem identifies a bias-controlled change in the dominant adsorption geometry for every target occupancy and quantitatively classifies the critical exponent, including an all-history degeneracy at the transition. The output is a structural classification rather than recomputation of finite-shell tables or a generic beta tail.
